articles.title: 1001 Threads of Mizan: The First Preview
articles.summary: While I can definitely see it working well solo, playing with two other players in real time is where 1001 Threads of Mizan really shines. There were no multiplayer quick time events or big flashy mid-fight cutscenes that triggered when everyone did a specific thing, but there were definitely…
body: From the very start of my demo it was obvious that 1001 Threads of Mizan’s developer MBC Game Studio is taking its source material seriously in an effort to make something that’s unique and interesting. After the intro cutscene, there was barely any chatter between the three main characters, and most of the world-building and story was handled by a narrator, Shahrazad, who is the actual storyteller in the book One Thousand and One Nights that 1001 Threads of Mizan is based on. 1001 Threads is rich with its source material, and it was great seeing an action-adventure game take place in a time period that isn't really covered that often in AAA games.

articles.title: Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons Doesn’t Seem Too Concerned With The “D&D” Part Of Its Title
articles.summary: After nearly a year of silence, Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons has reemerged to give sword and sorcery fans a first look at its third-person gameplay. Warlock's gameplay reveal came during Gamescom Opening Night Live, and featured a lengthy trailer showcasing how the game's spell-slinging combat will…
body: Based on its latest trailer, Warlock forgoes sticking to the same formula many D&D-based adventure games tend to use, placing an emphasis on spells and combat rather than roleplay and replicating the tabletop experience. This might not appeal to those seeking a more traditional D&D-like experience--or those who are baffled by main character Katri's seemingly infinite spell slots--but its dark fantasy visuals, snappy spellcasting, and Witcher-esque gameplay certainly look fun.

In addition to a first look at gameplay, the trailer also gave us a bit more information regarding the game's setting. It seems as though Warlock will follow Katri's journey through Ravenloft's Domains of Dread. Darkon, the largest and most powerful of these domains, was seen in the trailer; we can only hope that a Darklord Azalin appearance will follow.

Warlock was announced during the 2025 The Game Awards via a stylish heavy metal trailer that spotlighted the game's main character, Katri. In an interview last year, developer Invoke Studios said players will always play as Katri, but may meet other characters and form alliances with them while adventuring.

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Campaign Hands-On Preview: To Quote Marcus Fenix, “Nice”
articles.summary: I’m now not only more fired up to finish Gears of War: E-Day’s prequel story than ever, but I’m also more confident than ever that, at least based on the small slice I’ve played so far, E-Day has struck the exact right balance of tried-and-true old stuff and compelling new stuff.
body: I’m a massive fan of Gears of War, as I have been since the very beginning. But I have to be honest: something about Gears of War: E-Day’s campaign reveal at the Xbox Showcase a couple months ago just didn’t quite land right with me. It wasn’t bad, by any stretch of the imagination. But I just wasn’t as fired up as I thought I’d be after seeing the first new Gears of War campaign footage in seven years (OK, six if we’re counting Hivebusters).

When I finally sat down to play E-Day’s campaign, though, it took all of about 30 seconds to turn my tepid feelings into joyful smiles. My one-hour preview, which covered the early parts of Act 2, featured plenty of everything I want from and love about Gears of War: Marcus Fenix, Dominic Santiago, lots of story cutscenes, a sweet mix of old weapons and new ones (including the origin story for a signature Gears firearm known for its sharp teeth), some evolved gameplay mechanics, killer setpieces, new Marcus Fenix one-liners, subtle references to characters we know and love, and did I mention Marcus Fenix saying and doing cool sh*t?

articles.title: Roco Kingdom Goes Global
articles.summary: Since its launch in China in March 2026, Roco Kingdom has made a huge mark on the country's app charts. The game went straight to the top among new mobile titles, both in terms of average daily active users and revenue.
body: If you've never heard of Roco Kingdom, that's because the franchise has spent most of its 16-year life in China, where it's seen huge success. What started as a browser game in 2010 has since spawned four feature films, a long-running animated series, and over 100 published books. The game itself has had more than 350 million registered players across its history.

Roco Kingdom is a multiplayer open-world creature-collecting game where players take on the role of a Roco, setting out to explore the sprawling continent of Carosia to befriend its native creatures, called Jinies. There are over 400+ of them at launch, and no two are quite the same: every Jini has its own unique height, weight, and habits, interacting with the world around them in ways that make the environment feel variable and dynamic.

Developed by Morefun Studios, known for extraction shooter Arena Breakout: Infinite, the latest game has been in development for the last six years. The world itself is built around natural habitats, with distinct landscapes and climates shaping where different Jini species live and behave with the outcome being a living ecosystem rather than a static backdrop.

articles.title: Metro 2039 Explores The Horror Humans Can Commit In Latest Gameplay Trailer
articles.summary: The Metro games have never shied away from shoving players into a bleak post-apocalyptic world, but in Metro 2039, things are looking especially grim. Ahead of its release in 2027, a new gameplay trailer for Metro 2039 was revealed at Gamescom Opening Night Live, showing how players will have to…
body: The gameplay showcased several hallmarks of the Metro's distinct action. These include dangerous metro tunnels filled with soldiers, monsters inhabiting the radiation-filled surface, and the many, many guns you'll have to dispatch them with. Like previous entries, you'll be able to craft weapons to suit your playstyle, with the gameplay showcasing an aggressive approach to the series' stealth action.

While Metro 2039 still features mutated monsters and ghouls, it seems 4A Games is focusing more on the atrocities humans can commit in this sequel. As described by developers on stage at Opening Night Live, Metro 2039 is about consequences: the cost of silence, the horror of tyranny, the price of freedom. It is clear the studio is drawing from its experience of developing the sequel while enduring the ongoing war in Ukraine.

articles.title: NBA 2K27 Teases GTA 6 Crossover Of Some Kind
articles.summary: 2K Sports has released a new trailer for NBA 2K27 today, and it features a reference to GTA 6 that is prompting people to theorize about what it may mean. The Season 1 trailer for NBA 2K27 does a lot more than just show off what's coming in Season 1--it also hints at Seasons 2 and 3.
body: As you can see in the trailer below, the imagery and styling for Season 3 is plainly referencing GTA 6 with its palm trees, font, and colors. Police sirens can be heard as well, which is another nod to GTA.
The video doesn't specifically state when NBA 2K27's Season 3 will begin. However, it does confirm that Season 2 starts October 16.
If seasons are as long as they have historically be in the past, that would mean Season 3 could start around the end of November. And that lines up nicely with GTA 6's release on November 19.

This isn't the first time that GTA 6 and basketball have been connected. One of the GTA 6 gameplay leaks showed main character Jason dribbling a basketball and shooting hoops at his house, with many taking this to mean basketball will be a minigame of sorts in GTA 6.

articles.title: Paradox's latest grand strategy Afterworld wants you to survive the post-apocalypse
articles.summary: After a succession of grand strategy sequels - including Crusader Kings 3, Victoria 4, and Europa Universalis 5 - Paradox has unveiled Afterworld, its first grand strategy game to feature an original setting in over a decade.
body: As its name hints at, Afterworld whisks strategy fans to a post-apocalyptic future; specifically a post-apocalyptic North America blighted with hazardous terrain, dangerous old-world ruins, and the desperate remnants of humanity. Through this hostile, procedurally generated landscape, players must slowly grow a small group of survivors into a continent-spanning empire - by first scavenging food, water, and shelter, before rediscovering the basic methods of civilisation and expanding from there.

Paradox describes Afterworld as a "story rich" strategy game, which begins with players choosing one of several origin stories for their group - perhaps they've been forced to abandon a failed nuclear bunker, or are "wayward zealots looking for their goddess in the dustlands". Then as the group grows, they'll learn new skills and rediscover technologies (all unlocked dynamically based on what players find as they explore), set up convoys and supply lines, encounter rival groups, negotiate trades,and fight where necessary.

articles.title: Ananta’s New Trailer Goes Hard On Memes
articles.summary: Today, during Gamescom Opening Night Live, NetEase showed off new gameplay for Ananta, its upcoming open-world anime action-adventure. The trailer featured multiple cityscapes, a January 15 release date, and... internet memes?
body: Indeed, the gameplay was highlighted by multiple references to internet jokes and slang, including the Gatsby lifting glass meme, the Dragon Ball Z "Yamcha death" meme, and the main hero being called the "yeetmaster."

Outside of the jokes, the three-minute trailer showed both Nova City and Lingyun City, the two open areas that will make up Ananta's setting. We see traversal via flying car, motorbike, skateboard, and more as the "yeetmaster" meets multiple characters and get into some close calls while traveling through both cities.

Ananta will see players take the role of a single influncer with the goal of saving the world by "going viral." The influencer will meet over 100 characters throughout the quest, each with their own individual questlines, and some can be recruited as allies along the way.
For more on Gamescom, check out our coverage on Ubisoft's Rainbow Six Tactics, Hoyoverse's Nodusfall, and the return of Roller Coaster Tycoon.

Geralt has new toys, including a hookshot-like weapon that harks back to the first game in the trilogy. To get folks ready for the new DLC, CD Projekt Red said that it will be making both of the game's DLC totally free to play. The hope is that the last DLC will ensure that Geralt goes out with a bang.

articles.title: Every Big Announcement from Gamescom Opening Night Live
articles.summary: We might not have E3 anymore, but at least we have Gamescom. The Cologne, Germany-based gaming extravaganza is the summer's last must-see event before a busy fall season packed with new game releases.
body: From The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Songs of the Past to Tides of Annihilation, Gamescom Opening Night Live was packed with exciting announcements and trailers. Here’s a breakdown of the biggest games that were showcased.

CD Projekt Red closed the show with the upcoming The Witcher 3 expansion, which will be released in 2027 — a full 12 years after the base game came out. In its first trailer, we got an idea of Songs of the Past ’s story and a new chain weapon for Geralt. A developer joined host Geoff Keighley on stage and said Songs of the Past would be Geralt's "last adventure" before the series passes the torch to Ciri. The Witcher 4 wasn’t shown off, but at least we know CDPR is targeting a 2028 release window for Ciri’s new adventure.

The Witcher 3 is also getting a remaster with upgraded visuals, new finishers, expanded photo mode, new Signs FX, and so much more. It'll be a free upgrade for all The Witcher 3 owners on Sept. 29. Also, the previous expansions Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine will be made free for all players starting Tuesday.
points: We might not have E3 anymore, but at least we have Gamescom.

articles.summary: The Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past - which is due to arrive 12 years after the base game was released - has finally been detailed in a debut trailer, but the big news is there's also a The Witcher 3 remaster coming, and it'll be free upgrade for all existing owners of the game.
body: CD Projekt Red also gave us a glimpse of Songs of the Past as the closing trailer of Gamescom's Opening Night Live showcase this evening. The trailer showed "enhanced combat", "improved traversal and movement", "enhanced monster behaviours", a revamped skill tree and transmog for you gear, plus new finishers and a whacking great list of more that whistled past.
As well as all this, the two existing expansions for The Witcher 3 - Blood and Wine and Hearts of Stone - are also free for all owners of the base game as of this evening, too.

As for the expansion, this is our first proper dose of Songs of the Past information since The Witcher 3 expansion was announced in May this year. All we knew about it then was that it starred Geralt, would be equivalent in size to the game's other expansions, was being co-developed by external studio Fool's Theory, and would release in 2027. Everything else about Songs of the Past - setting, timeframe, storyline - was speculation.

articles.title: Guy Ritchie's 9/10 Action Thriller Is Officially One of His Best Movies on Streaming
articles.summary: Guy Ritchie has spent decades bouncing between crime capers, spy thrillers, and blockbuster franchises, but one of the filmmaker's most acclaimed movies feels remarkably different from the projects that made him famous.
body: Guy Ritchie's The Covenant is one of the filmmaker's best-reviewed pictures, and it's now getting a new lease on life streaming on Hulu. In the picture, Jake Gyllenhaal stars as Sergeant John Kinley, an American soldier on a tour of duty in Afghanistan. Featuring local interpreters, the film draws on stories and plot threads largely inspired by true events.

What makes Guy Ritchie's The Covenant particularly interesting within his larger filmography is that it tends to abandon the filmmaker's usual bag of tricks. Those looking for Ritchie's typical fast-talking British gangsters or the heightened blockbuster antics seen in Sherlock Holmes won't find much of it here. Instead, Ritchie delivers a surprisingly straightforward war thriller built nearly entirely around the relationship between two men.

articles.title: After 2 Hours, Gears of War: E-Day's Campaign Goes BRRRR In All the Right Ways | Preview
articles.summary: This is not meant as an admonishment. If anything, it’s praise: Gears of War: E-Day, at least based on a two-hour Xbox Series X build of its campaign I recently played, seems to have fully understood the Gears of War assignment.
body: Out Oct. 6 for Windows PC and Xbox Series X, Gears of War: E-Day is the first Gears of War game in seven years. It’s a prequel, detailing the events of “Emergence Day,” or “E-Day” — the titular event where a horde of locust-like creatures, called the Locust Horde, emerge from the core of the planet and start wreaking bloody, brutal havoc, killing 25% of the human population overnight. You play as Marcus Fenix, the protagonist of the original trilogy, and are joined by Dominic Santiago, also a key character from the original trilogy.

At face value, Gears of War: E-Day is Gears of War. As I detailed in a July preview of its Horde mode (where you fight against waves of increasingly challenging enemies), the core mechanics here are quintessential Gears of War. The lumbering gravity. The conveniently waist-height architecture seemingly designed for ducking behind. The satisfying brrrr of landing a chainsaw melee attack. That reloading minigame! It’s all here. Building on its excellent work with Gears of War 4 and Gears 5, developer The Coalition has once again captured the classic Gears essence in a bottle.
points: If anything, it’s praise: Gears of War: E-Day, at least based on a two-hour Xbox Series X build of its campaign I recently played, seems to have fully understood the Gears of War assignment.

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day somehow feels exactly like a direct continuation of the original Xbox 360 trilogy, for better and for worse
articles.summary: Marcus Fenix says something gruffly, his squad laughs, then a horde of Locust enemies rushes the team. The hulking figure of Marcus roadie-runs towards the nearest hip-high bit of cover, slams his muscly shoulder into the concrete, and starts laying down suppressing fire with his Lancer machine…
body: But this isn't a bad thing. Even the post-trilogy Gears games have never really lived up to the series' high - that initial, unlikely run of hits between 2006 and 2011. Since the heady days of the early 2010s, there's not been something so unashamedly silly as Gears to keep us occupied. The days of the co-op over-the-shoulder cover shooter seem confined to the Xbox 360 and PS3 era, as the FPS ate away at its popularity in the generations between.

If you managed to get some time with the E-Day beta, you'll know the bones are solid enough; the shooting is good, the cover mechanics are decent, and the cover-to-cover wall bouncing is as controversial as it ever was. Movement exploits and 'cheesing' are as divisive now as they were in the 2010s. And therein lies my assessment of the single-player mode, too, really: if you like Gears back then, you're going to like this. If you didn't, precious little has changed.

videos.title: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 - Launch Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is available now for PS5! This is not a rescue mission, it’s a fight for survival. Xenomorphs stalk the corridors, ambush from the shadows, and swarm in overwhelming numbers. Every room could be your last.
body: #ps5 #ps5games #aliensfireteamelite
points: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is available now for PS5!
This is not a rescue mission, it’s a fight for survival.
Coordinate with your fireteam, leverage each class’s unique abilities, and adapt on the fly as encounters escalate from tense standoffs to all-out war.
With deeper squad mechanics, smarter enemies, and a fully customizable Specialist class, AFE2 delivers the definitive co-op Aliens experience.
videos.author: PlayStation
